title: Progress and rewards
summary: XP for real effort, the day done, streaks with freezes, achievements and a daily reminder.
description: Rewards that make daily practice a habit, and pay for what was really done.

stories.want: a streak that survives one missed day
stories.soThat: one bad day does not undo a month

stories.want: rewards only for what I actually did

requirements.text: A wrong answer that is not almost right earns no XP.

XP per right answer is what its kind of card pays (`xp.pick-meaning`, `xp.pick-word`, `xp.tiles-two`, `xp.tiles-all`, `xp.typed`, `xp.gaps-from-bank`), plus `xp.first-time` for an item answered the first time, times its level's factor (`xp.level-factor-a1` to `xp.level-factor-c`), rounded.

history.text: XP per right answer depends on the kind of exercise: recognising among choices pays 6, typing or dictation 14, filling a gap 16; an item answered for the first time pays 2 more.
history.reason: Harder kinds of card and harder material are worth more; the new, easier sentence cards pay less than the ones they lead to.

requirements.text: Extra practice on a lesson already passed today pays `xp.extra-share` of the XP.
A day is done when the day's lessons are all done and something was practised; on a day with no lessons to give, having practised at all.
A failed conversation or a quick game counts as having practised, even when it earned no XP.
The streak counts done days in a row and still shows as alive on the day after the last done day.
Each `streak.freeze-every` days of a streak earn a streak freeze; at most `streak.freezes-max` are kept.
Missed days are covered by freezes automatically when there are enough freezes for all of them.
A word sticks once its review interval reaches `word.sticks-at`.

Achievements are earned for done days and streaks (3, 7, 30 and 100 days), words met and words that stick, sentences, dialogues, passed conversation lessons, writing, listening, a first song, a lesson made by the tutor and a completed course.
An achievement's progress and its unlock come from the same count.

Reset progress erases reviews, days, the XP log, the mastery ledger, passes, mastery, streak freezes, achievements, check-ins and the tutor's conversations together; courses and their content are kept, closed courses stay closed, and the learning log is kept.

deprecation.reason: The owner removed Reset progress: nobody needed it, and it left closed courses holding lessons that were no longer mastered.

requirements.text: AI costs survive a reset of progress.

deprecation.reason: Reset progress was removed, so there is no reset for costs to survive.

requirements.text: A reminder is scheduled once a day for the week ahead at a time the learner chooses; today's is skipped once the day is done.
Reminders are scheduled again on every launch.
The Progress screen shows stats, what has been met, achievements, XP by day, an 18-week activity map and vocabulary totals.

values.description: The review interval at which a word sticks.
What picking a meaning or a picture pays (`pick-meaning`, `pick-picture`).
What picking the word, or tiles with the endings set, pays (`pick-word`, `tiles-set`).
What tiles with two endings to choose, or a dictation from a word bank, pays (`tiles-two`, `bank-dictation`).
What tiles with every form, or a word written from hearing, pays (`tiles-all`, `hear-word`).
What typing a word, a dictation, a typed gap or saying it aloud pays (`type-word`, `dictation`, `gap-typed`, `say-word`, `say-sentence`).
What filling gaps from a word bank pays (`gaps-from-bank`).
What an item answered for the first time adds.
The share of its XP that extra practice pays.
